chunks: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to me from Abi Dawud al-Mustariq, from Umm Sa'id al-Ahmasiyyah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
He asked me, 'O Umm Sa'id, do you visit the grave of al-Husayn?' I said, 'Yes.' He said to me, 'Visit him, for verily the visitation of the grave of al-Husayn is obligatory upon men and women.'
ai.seo_question: Is visiting the grave of Imam Husayn obligatory for men and women in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) explicitly elevates the visitation of Imam al-Husayn’s (a.s.) grave from a recommended act to a mandatory obligation (wajib) for both men and women, underscoring its universal significance in Shia piety. This ruling reflects the broader theological view that the Imams’ graves serve as spiritual centers where believers connect with divine authority, making their visitation a continuous duty rather than a seasonal ritual.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 3. Muḥammad ibn Ja’far Al-Razzāz narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain ibn Abil Khaťťāb, from Abī Dāwūd Al-Mustariq, from Um Sa’īd Al-Aḥmasiyyah, who said:

Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) asked me, “O Um Sa’īd! Do you go to the Ziyārah of the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.)?” I replied, “Yes.” Imam (a.s.) said, “Go to his Ziyārah, for verily going to the Ziyārah of the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.) is WĀJIB (mandatory) on both men and women.”
